extracted.intended_audience: organisations (universities, research institutions, businesses/SMEs and other socio‑economic actors) preparing MSCA Doctoral Networks proposals and prospective doctoral candidates seeking MSCA-funded PhD vacancies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting proposals for Marie Skłodowska‑Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Networks: formation of eligible consortia, programme design requirements, researcher eligibility, funding scope, durations, and how to apply or find funded PhD vacancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of Doctoral Networks
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of Doctoral Networks is to implement doctoral programmes by partnerships of organisations from different sectors across Europe and beyond to train highly skilled doctoral candidates, stimulate their creativity, enhance their innovation capacities and boost their employability in the long-term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctoral programmes should respond to well-identified needs in various research and innovation areas, expose researchers to both academic and non-academic sectors, and offer research training as well as transferable skills and competences relevant for innovation and long-term employability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Doctoral Networks (standard / Industrial / Joint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctoral Networks can be standard, Industrial Doctorates or Joint Doctorates, each with specific features and incentives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial Doctorates and Joint Doctorates have additional, specific conditions (see their entries). Proposals should indicate which type is being implemented and adapt programme design accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Doctorates requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial Doctorates train PhD candidates who wish to develop their skills and step outside academia, in particular in industry and business. Individual participants must be enrolled in a doctoral programme and jointly supervised by the academic and non-academic partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Industrial Doctorates researchers should spend at least 50% of their time outside academia (see researcher eligibility entry). Joint supervision by academic and non-academic partners is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Doctorates requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint Doctorates provide a highly integrated type of international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary collaboration in doctoral training leading to a joint doctoral degree or multiple doctoral degrees awarded by the participating institutions. PhD candidates must be enrolled in a joint programme and be jointly supervised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint Doctorate projects have specific duration and fellowship length exceptions (project up to 5 years; fellowships up to 48 months). Proposals must demonstrate integrated collaboration and arrangements for awarding joint or multiple degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium composition and applicant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctoral Networks are open to international consortia of universities, research institutions, businesses, SMEs and other non-academic organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortia should include at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, with at least one of them established in an EU Member State. On top of this minimum, other organisations from any country in the world can also join. Specific conditions apply for Industrial and Joint Doctorates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctoral Networks can last for up to 4 years (up to 5 years in the case of Joint Doctorate projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must respect the maximum project duration depending on the Doctoral Network type (standard vs joint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration of each fellowship is between 3 and 36 months (between 3 and 48 months in the case of Joint Doctorate fellowships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship lengths in the proposal must fall within these ranges and note the exception for Joint Doctorates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum recruitment per beneficiary
rubrics_metrics.description: Each beneficiary must recruit at least one doctoral candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiaries may also organise secondments for recruited doctoral candidates anywhere in the world; recruitment commitments should be explicit in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher eligibility: degree and enrolment
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers funded by Doctoral Networks must not have a doctoral degree at the date of their recruitment and should be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility screening must ensure candidates do not already hold a doctorate and are formally enrolled in an appropriate doctoral programme throughout the funded period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers can be of any nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no nationality restriction on recruited researchers, but mobility and enrolment criteria still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Doctorate time‑outside‑academia requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For Industrial Doctorates, researchers should spend at least 50% of their time outside academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and secondment plans should document the non-academic component to demonstrate the 50% outside‑academia requirement is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility rule for recruited researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should comply with the mobility rules: in general, they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobility eligibility must be checked at recruitment; short stays (holidays, compulsory national service) are typically excluded but the rule is strict about main activity over the 36‑month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances and funded cost categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU provides support for each recruited researcher in the form of a living allowance, a mobility allowance and, if applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances. In addition, funding is provided for research, training and networking activities, management and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should budget and justify requested allowances and project costs under these eligible categories following the call documentation and applicable grant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission restriction (score threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: As from 2022, resubmission restrictions will apply for applications that received a score below 80% the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must check prior-year scores and the call rules before resubmitting; a score below 80% imposes restrictions (see the call page for exact resubmission policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission procedure and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to MSCA Doctoral Networks can be submitted from the opening date of the chosen call, and the completed proposal, including all annexes, should be submitted by the specified submission deadline of the chosen call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find open/forthcoming calls on the funding page and use the Funding & Tender Opportunities Portal to find partners and apply. All relevant documents (MSCA work programme, general annexes, guide for applicants, specific FAQs, application and evaluation forms, online manual on how to submit an application) are available on the dedicated call page on the Portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: How researchers find funded PhD vacancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates wishing to apply for PhD positions under Doctoral Networks should apply to funded Doctoral Network projects by consulting their open vacancies advertised internationally, including on the EURAXESS portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EURAXESS lists vacancies (updated daily); candidates will find the full requirements of positions, can apply directly to institutions or projects, and can find advice about visas, pensions, taxation, recognition of qualifications and other issues related to working as a researcher abroad.
